paper_title: An analysis of vaccine-related sentiments from development to deployment   of COVID-19 vaccines
caption: : Polarity scores for Australia
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the distribution of sentiment polarity scores for Australia by showing how the count of observations varies across polarity score values. The x-axis is labeled “Polarity scores” and uses a linear scale spanning roughly from −1.1 to 0.6, with regularly spaced tick labels at about 0.2 intervals (e.g., −1.0, −0.8, …, 0.6). The y-axis is labeled “Counts” on a linear scale from 0 to 140,000, with tick marks every 20,000. A single blue solid line with circular markers connects the values across polarity scores: counts are near zero at the most negative scores (around −1.1 to −0.7), rise to a few thousand near −0.6, then increase to around 17,000 near −0.5 before dipping to roughly 9,000 near −0.35; the series then climbs through approximately 25,000 near −0.3 and about 41,000 near −0.2, reaches about 92,000 near −0.1, and peaks near 134,000 at approximately 0.0. After the peak, it drops to about 56,000 near 0.1, rises again to around 72,000 near 0.2, then declines to roughly 26,000 near 0.3 and to only a few thousand near 0.4, shows a smaller rise near 0.45 (around 22,000), and ends near 0.55 at close to 1,000.
